answers.text: Fixed format: drop-off time, pallet count, then any damage, in that order. That's what keeps it the same each time.
Time, customer, topic, outcome for each entry, then count how many need following up at the end.
Something's off with the finishing time on that one — doesn't quite fit with the start time. Worth flagging before it's filed.
118 versus 96 is more like a 23% rise, not the 20% they've put — I'd get that corrected.
Output 2 for me, it shows the 940 and 827 behind the 88%, so you can see where it comes from.
Email 2, since it gives the actual volume numbers to back up asking for the better rate. Email 1 doesn't say where 'we'd expect a better rate' comes from.
1. No, home address, not going in. 2. Yes. 3. No, unsigned budget stays out. 4. Better to leave that too. 5. No.
I'd hold back the rates and the retainer cap, and be careful with the NDA clause since it names the client. The general scope of the work is probably fine to paste as is.
I'd build in a check where a sample of the reconciled lines gets matched back to the warehouse records before the summary goes out — that would catch a wrong total, not just a typo.
Reading the invoice PDF is the risky step, and the gate should really sit before the note is auto-submitted.
